questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Which cloud model generally supplies a managed business application?
questions.explanation: SaaS supplies application functionality as a service.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Which model generally leaves more operating-system responsibility with the customer than PaaS?

choices.text: Software as a service in every case.

questions.explanation: IaaS generally exposes more of the infrastructure software stack to customer administration.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: What does a hybrid cloud deployment combine?

choices.text: Distinct deployment environments connected for the organization’s needs.
A guarantee that no vendor is used.

questions.explanation: Hybrid deployment combines environments; it is not itself a control guarantee.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Who remains responsible for appropriate customer user-access configuration in a SaaS arrangement when the contract assigns it to the customer?

choices.text: The provider regardless of the stated responsibility.

questions.explanation: Shared responsibility follows the actual service and agreement.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: A system diagram omits the interface carrying sales data into the ledger. What is the concern?

choices.text: Important data-flow and control dependencies may be missed.
No concern if the ERP is expensive.
The missing interface proves all data is correct.

questions.explanation: Financial-reporting risks can arise in omitted interfaces.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: A company moves to a reputable cloud provider. What is still needed?

choices.text: Automatic elimination of all control work.
Vendor oversight and evaluation of retained and outsourced controls.
A presumption that every configuration is secure.

questions.explanation: Provider reputation does not replace governance and controls.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Assign control responsibilities and identify a missing dependency in an outsourced payroll system. Contract summary: The SaaS provider operates application infrastructure. The customer approves employee master-file changes, grants user roles, and reconciles payroll totals. Architecture review: A third-party interface sends payroll journals to the general ledger, but the interface is absent from the documented data-flow diagram. Required: Application service model.
questions.explanation: The provider supplies the managed application.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Assign control responsibilities and identify a missing dependency in an outsourced payroll system. Contract summary: The SaaS provider operates application infrastructure. The customer approves employee master-file changes, grants user roles, and reconciles payroll totals. Architecture review: A third-party interface sends payroll journals to the general ledger, but the interface is absent from the documented data-flow diagram. Required: Owner of customer role approvals.
questions.explanation: The contract assigns customer access controls to the customer.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Assign control responsibilities and identify a missing dependency in an outsourced payroll system. Contract summary: The SaaS provider operates application infrastructure. The customer approves employee master-file changes, grants user roles, and reconciles payroll totals. Architecture review: A third-party interface sends payroll journals to the general ledger, but the interface is absent from the documented data-flow diagram. Required: Required response to the omitted interface.

choices.text: Document the data flow and evaluate its controls

questions.explanation: The interface is a relevant dependency.

questions.topic: IT Architecture, Cloud Models & Shared Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Assign control responsibilities and identify a missing dependency in an outsourced payroll system. Contract summary: The SaaS provider operates application infrastructure. The customer approves employee master-file changes, grants user roles, and reconciles payroll totals. Architecture review: A third-party interface sends payroll journals to the general ledger, but the interface is absent from the documented data-flow diagram. Required: Effect of outsourcing on accountability.

choices.text: It changes control performance but does not eliminate accountability

questions.explanation: Governance and retained responsibilities continue.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: What is a central purpose of an ERP?

choices.text: Integrate information and processing across business functions.
Guarantee every source transaction is valid.

questions.explanation: ERP integration connects business processes and data.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Which is an application control?
questions.explanation: The match validates processing within an application.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Which is generally an IT general control?

choices.text: Only counting a particular inventory item.
Controlled promotion of authorized program changes.

questions.explanation: Change management supports the reliability of systems and applications.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Does blockchain storage guarantee the truth of information originally entered?

choices.text: Yes, every off-chain fact is verified automatically.
Only if the chain has many nodes.

questions.explanation: Integrity of stored records does not prove the validity of source facts.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: An automated control uses an incorrect tax-rate configuration for every sale. What is the implication?

choices.text: Consistent automated processing can create systematic error.
No testing of configuration is needed.
All financial statements must automatically be correct.

questions.explanation: Automation can scale a configuration error across the population.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Before relying on an RPA-generated reconciliation, what should be evaluated?

choices.text: Only whether the output is a PDF.
Input completeness, logic, exception handling, and review.
A presumption of independence because it is automated.

questions.explanation: Reliability requires validating the process and its dependencies.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Identify controls and weaknesses in an automated payment workflow. Process flow: The ERP matches invoices with orders and receipts. Vendor bank-account changes can be made and approved by the same user. A robot exports payment totals but drops rejected records from its report. Control objective: Payments should be authorized, directed to valid recipients, completely recorded, and reconciled. The matching rule alone does not address every objective. Required: Classification of the three-way match.
questions.explanation: The match controls a specific transaction-processing function.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Identify controls and weaknesses in an automated payment workflow. Process flow: The ERP matches invoices with orders and receipts. Vendor bank-account changes can be made and approved by the same user. A robot exports payment totals but drops rejected records from its report. Control objective: Payments should be authorized, directed to valid recipients, completely recorded, and reconciled. The matching rule alone does not address every objective. Required: Vendor-change weakness.

choices.text: Lack of independent authorization or segregation

questions.explanation: Self-approved master-data changes can redirect payments.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Identify controls and weaknesses in an automated payment workflow. Process flow: The ERP matches invoices with orders and receipts. Vendor bank-account changes can be made and approved by the same user. A robot exports payment totals but drops rejected records from its report. Control objective: Payments should be authorized, directed to valid recipients, completely recorded, and reconciled. The matching rule alone does not address every objective. Required: Risk from omitted rejected records.
questions.explanation: Rejected records may need investigation and reconciliation.

questions.topic: ERP, Business Processes, Interfaces & Automation
questions.prompt: Identify controls and weaknesses in an automated payment workflow. Process flow: The ERP matches invoices with orders and receipts. Vendor bank-account changes can be made and approved by the same user. A robot exports payment totals but drops rejected records from its report. Control objective: Payments should be authorized, directed to valid recipients, completely recorded, and reconciled. The matching rule alone does not address every objective. Required: Best next step.

choices.text: Trace inputs, exceptions, approvals, and postings through the full process
Assume the robot is an independent auditor

questions.explanation: End-to-end understanding connects each risk to an appropriate control.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: What does a data dictionary primarily describe?

choices.text: Data fields, meanings, formats, and related definitions.

questions.explanation: A dictionary supports consistent interpretation of data.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: What can an inner join do to unmatched records?
questions.explanation: Inner joins retain matching rows and can omit relevant unmatched records.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: Which analytical schema commonly has a central fact table with related dimension tables?
questions.explanation: A star schema structures facts and dimensions for analytics.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: What is a purpose of relational normalization?

choices.text: Guarantee every input fact is true.
Reduce certain redundancy and update anomalies.

questions.explanation: Normalization improves relational structure but is not a complete quality or security control.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: A $700 invoice appears twice after a one-to-many join. What is the overstatement if the result is summed without correction?
questions.explanation: The single $700 invoice is counted an extra time.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: An extraction excludes December 31 transactions through an incorrect date boundary. What is required?

choices.text: Accept the result because SQL ran successfully.
Correct the filter and validate the population against source controls.

questions.explanation: Execution success does not establish completeness or relevance.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: Evaluate a reporting extract before using it for financial analysis. Source and output: The source has 1,000 invoices totaling $500,000. The extract has 950 unique invoice IDs totaling $475,000 before a join. A customer-address join duplicates one $2,000 invoice. Query review: An inner join omits customers without an address, and the date filter excludes the last day of the period. Required: Number of source invoices missing before the join.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: Evaluate a reporting extract before using it for financial analysis. Source and output: The source has 1,000 invoices totaling $500,000. The extract has 950 unique invoice IDs totaling $475,000 before a join. A customer-address join duplicates one $2,000 invoice. Query review: An inner join omits customers without an address, and the date filter excludes the last day of the period. Required: Difference from the source total before the join.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: Evaluate a reporting extract before using it for financial analysis. Source and output: The source has 1,000 invoices totaling $500,000. The extract has 950 unique invoice IDs totaling $475,000 before a join. A customer-address join duplicates one $2,000 invoice. Query review: An inner join omits customers without an address, and the date filter excludes the last day of the period. Required: Additional overstatement caused by the duplicate invoice.
questions.explanation: One extra occurrence adds $2,000.

questions.topic: Data Integrity, Databases, SQL & Data Lifecycle
questions.prompt: Evaluate a reporting extract before using it for financial analysis. Source and output: The source has 1,000 invoices totaling $500,000. The extract has 950 unique invoice IDs totaling $475,000 before a join. A customer-address join duplicates one $2,000 invoice. Query review: An inner join omits customers without an address, and the date filter excludes the last day of the period. Required: Required remediation.

choices.text: Correct joins and filters and reconcile counts and totals

questions.explanation: Both omitted and duplicated records must be addressed.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: Which environment ordinarily hosts the live business system?
questions.explanation: Production supports live processing and requires controlled access and changes.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a rollback plan?

choices.text: Restore an appropriate prior state if a deployment fails.

questions.explanation: Rollback planning supports recovery from unsuccessful changes.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: Which test examines whether integrated components work together?
questions.explanation: Integration testing addresses interactions among components.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: What does a parallel conversion generally involve?

choices.text: Operating old and new systems concurrently for a period.

questions.explanation: Parallel operation supports comparison while increasing temporary effort and cost.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: A developer can change production payment logic without approval. What is the principal risk?

choices.text: No risk if version control exists.
Unauthorized or untested changes can affect live processing.

questions.explanation: Production access can bypass authorization, testing, and independent review.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: An emergency change lacks normal predeployment review. What should a controlled process include?

choices.text: Appropriate emergency authorization and timely retrospective review.
A permanent waiver of every control.

questions.explanation: Emergency procedures preserve accountability through adapted controls.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: Review a release process and identify the most appropriate control improvement. Release evidence: Code is stored in version control, but developers approve their own production deployments. No acceptance-test evidence is retained. Configuration changes are not logged. Emergency changes have no subsequent review. Objectives: Only authorized, tested, approved changes should reach production, and failures should be recoverable. Required: Improve deployment approval.

choices.text: Rely solely on the developer’s preference

questions.explanation: Independent authorization helps prevent self-approved changes.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: Review a release process and identify the most appropriate control improvement. Release evidence: Code is stored in version control, but developers approve their own production deployments. No acceptance-test evidence is retained. Configuration changes are not logged. Emergency changes have no subsequent review. Objectives: Only authorized, tested, approved changes should reach production, and failures should be recoverable. Required: Improve testing evidence.

choices.text: Retain relevant test results and acceptance approval

questions.explanation: Evidence should support whether acceptance criteria were met.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: Review a release process and identify the most appropriate control improvement. Release evidence: Code is stored in version control, but developers approve their own production deployments. No acceptance-test evidence is retained. Configuration changes are not logged. Emergency changes have no subsequent review. Objectives: Only authorized, tested, approved changes should reach production, and failures should be recoverable. Required: Improve configuration control.

choices.text: Ignore changes that are not code
Authorize, log, and monitor configuration changes

questions.explanation: Configuration can materially change system behavior.

questions.topic: SDLC, Change Management, Configuration & Releases
questions.prompt: Review a release process and identify the most appropriate control improvement. Release evidence: Code is stored in version control, but developers approve their own production deployments. No acceptance-test evidence is retained. Configuration changes are not logged. Emergency changes have no subsequent review. Objectives: Only authorized, tested, approved changes should reach production, and failures should be recoverable. Required: Improve emergency handling.

choices.text: Document emergency authorization and retrospective review

questions.explanation: Expedited changes still need accountable control.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: What does RTO describe?

choices.text: The targeted recovery time for restoring service.
The number of passwords in a file.

questions.explanation: Recovery time objective concerns restoration time.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: What does RPO describe?

choices.text: Only the time required to restart a server.

questions.explanation: Recovery point objective concerns how far back data recovery may go.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: A differential backup generally captures changes since which event?

choices.text: Only the immediately preceding incremental backup in every system.

questions.explanation: Differential backups accumulate changes since the full backup.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: Why is replication not a complete substitute for protected backups?

choices.text: It guarantees every file is valid.
It can replicate corruption or destructive changes.

questions.explanation: Replication may faithfully propagate unwanted changes.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: A four-hour RTO and one-hour RPO apply. Recovery takes two hours but uses data five hours old. What is the result?

choices.text: RTO is met; RPO is not.
RPO is met; RTO is not.

questions.explanation: Restoration time and data freshness must be evaluated separately.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: What provides stronger evidence of recoverability than a backup success notification alone?

choices.text: A tested restoration with measured results.

questions.explanation: Restore tests demonstrate whether usable data and services can be recovered within objectives.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: Compare recovery test results with business requirements. Requirements: RTO: 4 hours. RPO: 30 minutes. Agreed monthly service time: 40,000 minutes. Test and service results: Recovery took 3 hours. The restored dataset was 90 minutes old. Unplanned downtime during the month was 200 minutes. Required: Was the RTO met?.

choices.text: Only if all data is current

questions.explanation: Three hours is within the four-hour target.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: Compare recovery test results with business requirements. Requirements: RTO: 4 hours. RPO: 30 minutes. Agreed monthly service time: 40,000 minutes. Test and service results: Recovery took 3 hours. The restored dataset was 90 minutes old. Unplanned downtime during the month was 200 minutes. Required: Was the RPO met?.
questions.explanation: Ninety minutes exceeds the thirty-minute data-loss target.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: Compare recovery test results with business requirements. Requirements: RTO: 4 hours. RPO: 30 minutes. Agreed monthly service time: 40,000 minutes. Test and service results: Recovery took 3 hours. The restored dataset was 90 minutes old. Unplanned downtime during the month was 200 minutes. Required: Data-loss interval exceeding RPO, in minutes.
questions.explanation: 90 − 30 = 60 minutes beyond the target.

questions.topic: Availability, Backups, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
questions.prompt: Compare recovery test results with business requirements. Requirements: RTO: 4 hours. RPO: 30 minutes. Agreed monthly service time: 40,000 minutes. Test and service results: Recovery took 3 hours. The restored dataset was 90 minutes old. Unplanned downtime during the month was 200 minutes. Required: Availability percentage for the stated month.
